title: bug: local-runner-bridge.test.mjs I1 and I3 probe the agent child with a bare kill(pid, 0) right after the bridge supervisor exits, so a job the uncontained fixture leaves for PID 1 to reap reads as alive; I3 fails at :532 under load and CI's "Test local runner prerequisite bundles" step goes red at random (1 of 7 CI-shaped and 1 of 8 loaded runs on bc4793cf); sibling gap of task-b712ce09's S11 probe fix
description:
Filed by hunt #20 (task-9f3eac6d, a CI dry run of moe/work-2026-10-24 at bc4793cf). It goes in this epic because task-b712ce09, the S11 twin of this race, was filed and fixed here, and CQ-R (the bridge's own epic) is complete.

PROBLEM
- local-runner-bridge.test.mjs:443 defines `alive = pid => { try { process.kill(pid, 0); return true; } catch { return false; } }`. kill(pid, 0) succeeds for a zombie, and for a process that is still exiting.
- I1 (:493) and I3 (:532, once for each of its 16 cases) assert `alive(host.child) === false` straight after the supervisor's exit event or `host.end()`.
- `host.child` is the job's global pid (AGENT_CHILD :439).
- The test runs as non-root, so guest-supervisor.py runs uncontained (see the GUARD comment, :99-104). The guard forks init, init starts the job with Popen, and all three share the guard's process group.
- On exit 74 or 76, relay()'s `finally` (guest-supervisor.py:563-569) SIGKILLs that group, but `reap(child)` waits for the guard only. init and the job are reparented and reaped later by PID 1, so right after the supervisor's exit the job's pid can still exist.
- task-b712ce09 (DONE 11-02, fb32db90) fixed the same race for S11. Its probe counts a process as unable to run by CANNOT_RUN (:1220-1226): State Z or X, SIGKILL pending in ShdPnd, or PF_EXITING. Another sibling (:1172) polls up to 5 s for its pids to go.
- I1 and I3 got neither fix.

EVIDENCE (HEAD bc4793cf, every MOE_* var cleared, Linux node 24, WSL kernel 6.18)
- CI dry run, step "Test local runner prerequisite bundles" (its 14 files): exit 1 (tests 741, pass 737, fail 1, skipped 3). It ran in parallel with two other CI jobs. Log: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-9f3eac6d/ci/j4/08-local-runner.log
    test at scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs:517:1
    ✖ I3 an unknown, answered or malformed host response ends the bridge as a protocol violation (928.700442ms)
      AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: Expected values to be strictly equal:
      true !== false
          at TestContext.<anonymous> (file:///.../scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs:532:12)
- The same file alone, unloaded: 6 of 6 runs pass (90 pass, 1 skipped). Logs: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-9f3eac6d/ci/bridge-rerun-*.log
- With 16 busy-loop processes running, I1+I3 failed 1 of 8 runs at the same :532 assertion. Repro: `bash /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-9f3eac6d/mine/bridge-load-repro.sh <snapshot root> [runs] [burners]`; it kills only the burner PIDs it records. Logs: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-9f3eac6d/ci/bridge-load-*.log

FIX DIRECTION
- Test-side. Give I1 and I3 the "gone" rule that S11 settled on: a pid is gone when it is reaped or its /proc view is CANNOT_RUN.
  - That means /proc/<pid>/status and /proc/<pid>/stat on Linux, with kill(pid, 0) elsewhere.
  - Alternatively, wait a bounded time for it to disappear, as :1172 does.
- Keep the final assertion that the job does not survive the bridge, and leave the exit-code assertions unchanged.
- Do not change relay(). Its contract (guest-supervisor.py:19-20) is to kill the child group before the stream ends, not to reap every descendant.

FILES: scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs only. Not held by any open row (lanes.js -v at 09:12Z).
PLACEMENT: no dependsOn. It is file-disjoint from 62ec51f1, 1dfec7a4 and bbd7ad2d.
definitionOfDone: I1 and I3 count the job pid as gone only when it is reaped or its /proc view cannot run (the S11 CANNOT_RUN rule), or after a bounded wait of at most 5 s, and still fail when the job is alive and runnable after that.

`bash /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-9f3eac6d/mine/bridge-load-repro.sh <snapshot root> 10` reports 0 of 10 failed runs on a Linux git-archive snapshot of the fix commit, and `node --test scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs` passes unloaded there.

The row's diff leaves scripts/local-runner/guest-supervisor.py unchanged, and the CI step's 14-file `node --test scripts/tests/local-runner*.test.mjs` command (as listed in ci.yml) exits 0 in that snapshot with every MOE_* var unset.

implementationPlan.description:
The fix (DoD 1), with your own Edit tool, in scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs only. This follows the filer's follow-up (comment-3b4a7351): reuse the zombie-aware probe the file already has, rather than porting the S11 CANNOT_RUN script.

Why: `running = pid => alive(pid) && (process.platform !== 'linux' || procState(pid)?.[0] !== 'Z')` (:1145, with procState at :1144) is what S9 polls for up to 5 s (:1172). relay() SIGKILLs the job group but reaps only the guard (guest-supervisor.py:559-566), so PID 1 reaps the job a moment later.

Edits:
- I1, :493: replace `assert.equal(alive(host.child), false);` with two lines: `for (let waited = 0; waited < 5000 && running(host.child); waited += 100) await sleep(100);` and `assert.equal(running(host.child), false);`. Put a one-line comment above them: `// relay() kills the job group but reaps only the guard: PID 1 reaps the job, so give it the S9 wait (:1172).`
- I3, :532, inside its per-case loop: the same two lines, without the comment.
- Keep :490's positive `assert.ok(alive(host.child), ...)` and every exit-code assertion unchanged.
- Do not move procState or running. They are module-scope consts, and the file has no top-level await, so node:test runs every body after module evaluation. Both new references also come after several awaits.
- Do not touch scripts/local-runner/guest-supervisor.py or relay(). Its contract (:19-20) is to kill the child group, not to reap every descendant.

This is test-only: no runtime code or error handling changes. sleep is already imported at :12.

A validated prototype of exactly this diff (+5/-2) passed the step 2 gate at 95d91dc2 in a scratch clone.

Verification, once (DoD 2 and 3). From the task worktree, run the checkRefs command exactly as written. Its fresh output is moe.complete_task's verification evidence: 'failed runs: 0/10', the b.log and c.log `ℹ tests/pass/fail/skipped` lines, and 'exit: 0'.

The command, in order:
1. Checks the diff is exactly the test file. That implies guest-supervisor.py is unchanged (DoD 3).
2. Archives HEAD with the edited file overlaid.
3. Runs `npm ci && npm run build` in the snapshot's packages/moe-daemon. local-runner-agents TY1 and local-runner-channel C4-C9 need a built daemon (mem:gotcha-daemon-linux-snapshot-gate).
4. Runs the bridge file unloaded.
5. Runs /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-9f3eac6d/mine/bridge-load-repro.sh 10 times under 16 burner processes. The script records the burner PIDs and kills only those (global rail: never pattern-kill).
6. Runs the CI step's 14-file `node --test` list, extracted verbatim from .github/workflows/ci.yml, with every MOE_* var unset (env -i).

Reference run on the prototype: 0/10 failed; bridge 91 tests (90 pass, 1 skipped); CI step 741 tests (738 pass, 3 skipped, 0 fail); about 2.5 min. Host load affects only the time.

On failure, fix the test edit; never weaken an assertion or raise the 5 s bound. Never run npm ci or a build in the shared checkout (project rail).

Self-review, the final step. Load the adversarial-self-review skill.

Check:
- The bound is real. In a scratch copy of the snapshot, temporarily change the I1 assertion to `assert.equal(running(process.pid), false)`, a live, runnable pid. I1 must FAIL after about 5 s, which proves the poll stops and the assertion still bites. Restore with `git show HEAD:scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs` plus your edit, and `cmp` before the final gate.
- I3's 16 cases wait only while the pid lingers (normally 0-200 ms each), so its 30_000 ms test timeout still holds. A truly surviving job fails at the first case after 5 s.
- The positive :490 check, the exit codes ([74, null] and [76, null]) and the observation check are byte-identical.
- No other line changed: the diff is +5/-2.

If anything changed, re-run step 2's command before moe.complete_task. Put the bound-check result in the completion summary.

comments.author: architect-cd0ac706
comments.content:
Filer's follow-up, re-derived at bc4793cf.

1) A cheaper fix than the one in the description already exists in this file.
   - `const running = pid => alive(pid) && (process.platform !== 'linux' || procState(pid)?.[0] !== 'Z')` is defined at :1145.
   - It is the zombie-aware probe that :1172 polls for up to 5 s: `for (let waited = 0; waited < 5000 && [...].some(running); waited += 100) await sleep(100)`.
   - Fix: give I1 (:493) and I3 (:532) the same bounded poll on `running(host.child)` before asserting that it is false.
   - `running` is a module-scope const, so the earlier tests can use it.
   - Port the S11 CANNOT_RUN rule only if the poll alone still flakes under bridge-load-repro.sh.
2) Line corrections:
   - CANNOT_RUN is at :1224-1227, not :1220-1226.
   - relay()'s finally block is guest-supervisor.py:559-566 (killpg at :563, reap at :566).
   - The GUARD comment is :99-104, and the exit-code contract is :19-20.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: I1 and I3 in scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs no longer flake under load. After the bridge supervisor exits, each waits at most 5 s (100 ms steps) for the job pid to stop being `running` (reaped, or a zombie on Linux; the file's existing S9 probe), then asserts it is not running. A job still alive and runnable after 5 s still fails the test. Test-only: no runtime code or error handling changes.
acceptanceCriteria: I1 (:493) and I3 (:532) use `for (let waited = 0; waited < 5000 && running(host.child); waited += 100) await sleep(100);` followed by `assert.equal(running(host.child), false);`.
bridge-load-repro.sh <snapshot> 10 reports 'failed runs: 0/10', and the bridge file passes unloaded in the snapshot.
The CI step's 14-file `node --test scripts/tests/local-runner*.test.mjs` list from ci.yml exits 0 in the snapshot with MOE_* unset, and guest-supervisor.py is unchanged.
invariants: Every other assertion in I1 and I3 is byte-identical (the :490 alive-while-running check, the exit codes, frames and observations).
The wait is bounded at 5 s per probe, and a runnable survivor still fails.
compatibility: S9 (:1172), S11's CANNOT_RUN probe and every other test keep their own probes unchanged.
reuse: `running` and `procState` (local-runner-bridge.test.mjs:1144-1145) and S9's bounded poll (:1172), as suggested in comment-3b4a7351; `sleep` imported at :12.
sourceAssumptions: local-runner-bridge.test.mjs:443 `alive` = bare kill(pid, 0); :493 and :532 assert alive(host.child) === false; :1144-1145 procState/running; no top-level await in the file.
guest-supervisor.py:559-566: relay()'s finally killpg()s the job group and reaps only the guard.
checkRefs: ( cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" && [ "$(git diff --name-only HEAD)" = scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs ] && S=$(mktemp -d) && git archive HEAD | tar -x -C "$S" && cp scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs "$S/scripts/tests/" && cd "$S" && X="env -i HOME=$HOME PATH=$HOME/.nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin:/usr/bin:/bin LANG=C.UTF-8" && (cd packages/moe-daemon && $X sh -c 'npm ci && npm run build' >/dev/null 2>&1) && $X node --test scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs > b.log 2>&1 && $X bash /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-9f3eac6d/mine/bridge-load-repro.sh "$S" 10 > l.log 2>&1 && grep -q '^failed runs: 0/10$' l.log && $X node --test $(sed -n 's/^ *run: node --test \(scripts\/tests\/local-runner\.test\.mjs .*\)$/\1/p' .github/workflows/ci.yml) > c.log 2>&1; E=$?; tail -1 l.log; grep -aE '^ℹ (tests|pass|fail|skipped) ' b.log c.log; echo "exit: $E"; exit $E )

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (1) Port S11's CANNOT_RUN /proc probe (the description's first idea): not needed. The file's own `running` probe plus S9's 5 s bounded poll covers the zombie and still-exiting windows, and the filer's follow-up (comment-3b4a7351) recommends it. Escalate to CANNOT_RUN only if the 10-run load repro still fails. (2) Reap the job in relay(): rejected. The supervisor's contract is to kill the group, not to reap descendants, and the row forbids touching guest-supervisor.py. (3) Moving procState/running up next to alive: unnecessary, because of TDZ safety (no top-level await; references come after awaits). It would only grow the diff.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- The same race was fixed for S11 by task-b712ce09 (fb32db90).
- S9 (:1172), S12 (:1273), :1414 and :1509 already use the `running` + 5 s poll idiom. I1 and I3 were the only `alive(...) === false` asserts left after a supervisor exit.
planningNotes.risks:
- The load repro runs 16 busy-loop burners on the shared host for about 1-2 min. It kills only its own recorded PIDs; do not substitute any pattern kill.
- RED is probabilistic: 1 of 8 loaded runs at bc4793cf, per the filer. The deterministic proof that the assertion still bites is step 3's live-pid bound check.
- The CI step needs the snapshot daemon built, or TY1 and C4-C9 fail for an unrelated reason.
